items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: I met this guy there, Ray Gorham, who was associated with a new club opening called The Showcase.

ctx.x: That's where our first record date came from. Then after we were there for a spell, we felt that we were ready now, had outgrown Seattle. And I was the business person in the group. I got in my car and drove to California, to represent the Mastersounds. I came down to Los Angeles and went to Pacific Jazz Records. Dick Bock. Dick heard the tapes, and he was so impressed with the tapes that we didn't have to re-record, no studio time or anything. He just bought that master and pressed it. The first album came out.

On my way back to Los Angeles (means Seattle), I'm bursting open inside. Stopped in San Francisco, and I spent time there scouting. I met this guy there, Ray Gorham, who was associated with a new club opening called The Showcase. And Ray was doing the booking for the new room.

And how we met up was, this whole thing was kiind of strange, but he bought the group to open his room. Brand new, opening, right? On Market Street, downtown Market Street in San Francisco. It turned out to be the first club that had... a teenager could get in because they didn't serve any booze. But it was a nightclub.
